messages:
maria: noticing spike in etcd read latency and controller-manager restarts in eu-west1, started ~10m ago
sam: saw it too, apiserver 5xxs around same time
kevin: any recent config changes or deploys?
jo: deploy-bot shows no full rollouts in the last hour, only a small metrics exporter bump by eng-andy ~12m ago
eng-andy: I pushed a prometheus scrape config tweak to kube-system metrics to increase scrape targets, forgot to rate-limit queries for /metrics from new exporter
maria: that fits — etcd read latency jumps coincide with heavy /metrics queries hitting kube-apiserver proxy to etcd
sam: controller-manager logs show watch reconnects and lease renew timeouts
kevin: also seeing GPU node attach operations queuing up; worker nodes in eu-west1 are slow to attach volumes (NVMe/GPU mounts)
jo: hypothesis: increased control plane load -> apiserver slow -> attach controller waits -> nodes stuck in NotReady -> GPUs idle and provisioning backlog grows
eng-andy: sorry about the scrape tweak, rolling back now
deploy-bot: rollback of configmap prometheus-scrape-kube-system initiated by eng-andy at 1728601300
maria: rolling back should help but we need immediate mitigation: can we throttle scrapes at the proxy ingress or add circuit breaker on kube-apiserver for heavy /metrics reads?
sam: temporary mitigation: add iptables rule to drop scrape source CIDR from exporter until rollback completes
kevin: I'll patch the firewall for the exporter IPs in eu-west1, doing now
kevin: patched. verifying pod states...
kevin: `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide | grep -E "apiserver|controller-manager"`
maria: apiserver CPU dropping back to normal, etcd read lat p99 down from 450ms -> 60ms
jo: controller-manager lease renews stabilizing, some older controller-manager pods still in crashloop but restarting fine
eng-andy: rollback confirmed applied at 1728601356, thanks for the quick rollback and firewall patch. sorry again
incident-bot: incident created: CP-2024-1234 - control-plane high read latency in eu-west1 at 1728601234
maria: we should add a rate-limit on /metrics path at the ingress in front of apiserver and also add Prometheus client-side rate limiting for heavy exporters
sam: +1. Also add an alert for exporter scrape-rate anomalies (high request rate to /metrics per minute)
kevin: GPU attach queue cleared after apiserver stabilized, provisioning backlog down from 42 -> 3 in 8m
jo: cost note: while backlog was stuck, Dedicated GPU pools reserved capacity had ~18 GPUs idling in eu-west1 for ~12m, approx $180 real-time cost impact, log that in the incident report
maria: added mitigation tasks to incident doc: add ingress rate-limit, exporter rate-limit, prometheus alert, postmortem owner assignment
eng-andy: I'll open a PR to add client-side rate limiting in the exporter and a config to prometheus to respect scrape_timeout and honor `max_concurrent_requests`
sam: we should also consider apiserver-side request prioritization for controller-manager traffic vs metrics scrapes — low-effort config first then long-term plan
kevin: is there any reason to scale etcd horizontally next time preemptively?
jo: scaling etcd isn't trivial; prefer fixing noisy clients and short-term throttles. if this becomes frequent we can look at read replicas and query isolation
maria: agreed. for now I'll declare incident mitigated when controller-manager restart rate < 2/min for 15m and GPU backlog remains <5
eng-andy: again, my bad. will followup with PR and a short blameless note in postmortem
kevin: monitoring graphs attached in incident doc (link) — will keep an eye for 1h
incident-bot: incident CP-2024-1234 status: mitigating -> monitoring at 1728601489
maria: thanks all, great triage. we'll run the postmortem template after the monitoring window
